## Initial review report

1. **Initial Git state:** Repository root confirmed as `C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap`. Working tree was clean on `codex/server-backup-restore`.
2. **Entire status:** Enabled and available in manual-commit mode.
3. **Branch synchronization:** Local branch and `origin/codex/server-backup-restore` both equal `36a8935485b0d8616036a7abcb3b4f18bd4f6756`. Local and remote `main` both equal `cfa4178f7b18f732b21cc433be57a65210a81130`.
4. **PR status:** PR [#9](https://github.com/five2seven/stackmap/pull/9) is open, draft, and has the expected head.
5. **GitHub Actions:** Run [30929874256](https://github.com/five2seven/stackmap/actions/runs/30929874256) completed successfully for the exact expected head.
6. **Diff summary:** One commit, 14 files, 794 additions and 14 deletions. No dependency, lockfile, generated-file, secret, Entire-configuration, or planning-record changes.
7. **Datastore authority:** SQLite remains authoritative. Server backup and restore use only the SQLite repository. IndexedDB access remains confined to legacy detection/export and its tests; no dual-write, fallback, synchronization, deletion, or Task 6 behavior was introduced.
8. **Backup schema:** Exact top-level version-1 shape and fail-closed version handling are implemented. Missing/unknown fields, primitives, arrays, nulls, and malformed nested records are rejected.
9. **Backup metadata:** Exact approved fields are enforced. Timestamps and revisions are validated; metadata remains informational and cannot overwrite target installation or database metadata. `applicationVersion` accepts any string, including empty strings, but is otherwise consistent with the documented shape.
10. **Export consistency:** **Important issue.** Revision, hosts, and services are read by separate queries without a read transaction, so a concurrent mutation can produce a mixed-revision backup.
11. **Host/service validation:** Complete exact-shape parsing, enums, nonblank IDs/names, safe revisions, and canonical timestamps are enforced.
12. **Nested identity:** Port/path shapes, values, ordering, and dependency validation are enforced. However, port and path IDs are incorrectly required to be globally unique rather than service-scoped.
13. **Referential integrity:** Missing hosts/dependencies, self-dependencies, duplicate dependencies, and malformed nested records are rejected before preview.
14. **Uploaded-object immutability:** Parsing creates new records and arrays; it does not sort, normalize, or rewrite the uploaded object.
15. **Preview API:** Fully validates before issuing a token, does not mutate inventory, and returns the approved summary and expected target revision.
16. **Token generation:** Uses 32 cryptographically random bytes encoded as an opaque base64url token.
17. **Token storage:** **Important issue.** The in-memory map has expiry cleanup but no capacity or rate bound; high-volume previews during the five-minute window can retain arbitrarily many complete validated backups.
18. **Backup-specific binding:** The validated backup is retained server-side with its token. Confirmation cannot substitute client data, and array order remains meaningful.
19. **Token expiry:** Five-minute expiry is enforced at the exact boundary and does not extend on confirmation attempts.
20. **Confirmation API:** Requires exactly `previewToken` and `expectedInventoryRevision`; unknown and malformed fields fail before mutation.
21. **Stale preview:** Transactional revision mismatch returns `RESTORE_PREVIEW_STALE`, leaves inventory unchanged, and requires re-preview.
22. **Invalid preview:** Missing, expired, consumed, and unknown tokens return a safe `RESTORE_PREVIEW_INVALID` conflict with request ID.
23. **Concurrent restore:** The process guard is released through `finally`; the SQLite transaction independently prevents two successful replacements. Cross-process lock contention may surface as a safe internal error rather than a stale conflict, but cannot produce two commits.
24. **Duplicate submission:** UI in-flight state blocks repeat clicks, and successfully consumed tokens cannot be reused. Token deletion follows the synchronous transaction commit; process restart discards all tokens.
25. **Atomic transaction:** Expected revision check, deletions, complete reinsertion, and global revision update occur in one SQLite transaction in foreign-key-safe order.
26. **Record identity/timestamps:** Host, service, port, and path IDs and host/service timestamps are preserved exactly. Dependencies use the existing service/dependency identity model.
27. **Record revisions:** Restored hosts and services are assigned revision 1; source revisions remain informational.
28. **Global inventory revision:** Success advances the target revision once; source revision is not copied. Overflow fails closed. Focused MAX_SAFE_INTEGER coverage is absent.
29. **Installation metadata:** Restore does not touch installation ID, database creation time, migrations, pragmas, WAL mode, or location.
30. **API errors:** Stable safe envelopes include code, message, and request ID. SQLite details, paths, stack traces, tokens, and backup contents are not returned.
31. **Fastify integration:** Routes precede static/SPA fallback and use the global API handler. Malformed JSON, unsupported media types, missing bodies, unsupported methods, and unknown API paths receive safe responses.
32. **Request/resource limits:** Preview has a 10 MiB body limit. Validation uses fixed-depth traversal, but token-store retention remains an avoidable resource-exhaustion risk.
33. **UI download:** Clearly labeled server backup download uses only `GET /api/v1/backup`, with a suitable filename and safe status handling.
34. **UI restore workflow:** JSON is parsed before preview; preview and confirmation are distinct; destructive acknowledgement is mandatory; confirmation is disabled in flight; cancel does not mutate inventory; success refreshes authoritative data.
35. **UI concurrency:** Stale/invalid conflicts clear the token, retain the selected file, require re-preview, and do not automatically retry.
36. **Legacy boundary:** Legacy export remains separate and unchanged. Schema-v3 legacy exports cannot pass the version-1 server parser. IndexedDB remains untouched.
37. **Container/workflow:** Exact-head CI verifies export, preview, confirmation, revision increment, nested inventory, installation ID, restart/recreation persistence, health, SQLite authority, non-root/read-only-root operation, writable `/config`, shutdown, and cleanup. It does not explicitly capture and assert `created_at` preservation across restore/recreation.
38. **Documentation:** **Minor issue.** README still says server restore is unimplemented, while architecture still describes restore as deferred and ambiguously calls version 3 the current JSON schema.
39. **Test coverage:** Core success, validation, stale, reuse, expiry, rollback, UI confirmation, browser sharing, restart, and recreation paths are covered. Missing risk-focused coverage includes coherent export during mutation, scoped nested IDs, preview-store bounds, simultaneous multi-connection restores, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and explicit container `created_at` preservation.
40. **Scope/exclusions:** No authentication, CORS, accounts, cloud/scheduled/incremental/partial/merge backup, legacy migration, Dexie removal, public demo, unrelated feature, Task 6, or planning advancement was added.

## Findings

41. **Blocking:** None.
42. **Important:**
   - Export can combine revision, hosts, and services from different inventory states.
   - Valid inventories containing the same port or path ID in different services cannot be restored, despite the database defining those identities as service-scoped.
   - Preview storage has no capacity bound and retains each complete validated backup.
43. **Minor:**
   - README and architecture contain stale, contradictory restore/schema statements.
   - Several required boundary and concurrency tests are absent, including explicit container `created_at` preservation.
44. **No issue:** Transaction rollback, target metadata isolation, revision reset, token randomness/expiry/single-use behavior, safe API envelopes, UI destructive confirmation, SQLite authority, and legacy-data isolation are sound.

## Validation

45. `npm run lint` — passed.
46. `npm test` — passed, 171 tests.
47. `npm run build` — passed.
48. `npm run test:e2e` — passed, 11 tests.
49. `npm audit --omit=dev` — passed, zero vulnerabilities.
50. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

## Final state

51. **Recommendation:** Changes required before merge.
52. No files were modified.
53. PR #9 remains draft and unmerged.
54. Task 6 was not started.
55. Planning records were not advanced.
56. Final working tree remains clean and synchronized with the remote feature branch.

A concurrent inventory mutation can therefore produce a backup whose metadata revision and record collections describe different states. Capture all three values in one SQLite snapshot transaction." file="C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap\server\backup.ts" start=100 end=104 priority=1}

::code-comment{title="[P1] Nested IDs are validated at the wrong scope" body="Ports and paths use composite database keys `(service_id, id)`, so their IDs only need to be unique within each service. Flattening every service here rejects backups that the authoritative schema and inventory API validly permit—including backups exported by this server. Move both uniqueness checks inside the per-service loop." file="C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap\server\backup.ts" start=140 end=141 priority=1}

::code-comment{title="[P1] Preview storage has no capacity bound" body="Every preview retains a complete parsed backup for five minutes, and cleanup only removes expired entries. Arbitrarily many valid preview requests can therefore consume memory proportional to request volume and backup size. Add a bounded capacity or equivalent admission/rate control with deterministic eviction." file="C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap\server\backup.ts" start=40 end=55 priority=1}

::code-comment{title="[P2] Public limitation contradicts implemented restore" body="This branch implements server-authoritative restore, but the limitations section still says it is not implemented. Update the statement so the public documentation matches the feature delivered by Task 5." file="C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap\README.md" start=134 priority=2}

::code-comment{title="[P2] Architecture still calls restore deferred" body="The current-implementation description says server restore remains deferred and describes version 3 as the current JSON schema, while this branch adds a separate server backup schema version 1 and restore workflow. Clarify the legacy schema versus server schema and remove the deferred claim." file="C:\Code\Projects\APP-StackMap\docs\architecture.md" start=7 priority=2}
